tools.name: runner__validate_config
tools.description: Validate THIS instance's config against its scenarios. Single-tenant: the server owns its one config, so pass ONLY instance_id — never a config path, and don't hunt for an argus-config.yaml; any other argument is refused (VR10-S1).

instance_id.description: REQUIRED on every tool (UC031/C8). The id of the instance this call is for, exactly as your environment names it (example: "orders-k3d"). This executor serves one instance and refuses the call when instance_id is omitted or names another instance.

tools.name: runner__run
tools.description: Run scenarios ASYNC (real argus/JMeter): returns {status:running, run_id} immediately - poll runner__get_report{run_id}. Selects a SUBSET by tag and/or layer (AND-applied). Syncs the set from the control-plane catalog first; if the CP is unreachable it REFUSES and offers use_local_scenarios rather than silently running what is on disk. Never pass run_id: the server mints it and returns it.

instance_id.description: REQUIRED on every tool (UC031/C8). The id of the instance this call is for, exactly as your environment names it (example: "orders-k3d"). This executor serves one instance and refuses the call when instance_id is omitted or names another instance.

layer.description: Optional. Run only the scenarios whose canonical layer is this one (example: "HTTP Ingestion"). Omitted: no layer filter.

scenario_ref.description: Optional. Run exactly one scenario, by its id (example: "ORDE-017"). Omitted: no single-scenario filter.

tag.description: Optional. Run only the scenarios carrying this tag (example: "smoke"). Omitted: no tag filter. Given together with layer, both must match.

use_local_scenarios.description: Optional, PLAN B only. Pass "true" ONLY after the control plane proved unreachable: run the scenarios on local disk anyway, accepting they were NOT verified against the catalog and may be stale. Omitted (the default): while the control plane is reachable this changes nothing; when it is unreachable the run refuses and waits instead.

tools.name: runner__get_report
tools.description: The report.json model for one WHOLE run, scoped to run_id when given (else the last run); product hat: expected values stripped. Find your scenario inside it — a per-scenario filter is not an argument.

instance_id.description: REQUIRED on every tool (UC031/C8). The id of the instance this call is for, exactly as your environment names it (example: "orders-k3d"). This executor serves one instance and refuses the call when instance_id is omitted or names another instance.

run_id.description: Optional. The run to report on, as returned by runner__run (example: "20260902T134305716"). Omitted: the last run on this instance. The report always covers the whole run — find your scenario inside it; there is no per-scenario filter.

tools.name: runner__get_sagas
tools.description: The saga timeline (what/why/by-whom) for a correlation id, from Loki.

correlation_id.description: The correlation id of one scenario execution, shaped tr-<run_id>-<SCENARIO>-<hash> (example: "tr-20260902T134305716-ORDE-017-3f9a1c"); read it from runner__get_report. Optional in the schema but needed for an answer: omitted, there is no id to match and nothing comes back.

instance_id.description: REQUIRED on every tool (UC031/C8). The id of the instance this call is for, exactly as your environment names it (example: "orders-k3d"). This executor serves one instance and refuses the call when instance_id is omitted or names another instance.

window.description: Optional. How far back to look, as a duration (example: "10m" or "15m"). Omitted: 10m. The window is a +/- band ANCHORED to the run when the correlation_id belongs to the last run (so a small window still finds an older run), else relative to now.

tools.name: runner__get_tail_logs
tools.description: Windowed, correlation-scoped log lines (== CLI tail-logs).

tools.name: runner__get_dashboard_url
tools.description: Grafana links: dashboard_url (scoped to correlation_id when given, else general) + overview_url (always the general dashboard). The URL is templated, not a check the run exists.

correlation_id.description: Optional. Deep-link the dashboard to this correlation id, shaped tr-<run_id>-<SCENARIO>-<hash> (example: "tr-20260902T134305716-ORDE-017-3f9a1c"). Omitted: the general dashboard.
